sources_note: Compiled entirely from the local snapshot mirror at sources/beast/ (six-locale mirror of beastofreincarnation.online) during this pass; no live web fetch was performed. Boss/weapon/mechanic facts are taken from the site's own launch guides, which in turn name their own primary sources (mainly Game8's tested boss tables at https://game8.co/games/Beast-of-Reincarnation/archives/613316, plus Game8/DualShockers for Crimson Malefact, Switchblade Gaming/Sportskeeda for Shidou & Nue, and two further Game8 articles cited by spirit-stones.html for its effect table and sell/keep guidance) -- those primary URLs are used as source_url where the citing page names one; fields backed only by this site's own cross-page synthesis (elemental-weaknesses/nushi-skills/combat-gauges/new-game-plus, plus the 3 weapon-type/Big Dipper facts) are marked source_tier:'onsite'. Achievement name/description/global-unlock-% is taken verbatim from sources/beast/achievements.json (Steam data captured 2026-09-14) and sources/beast/data/achievements-ja.json (official Japanese name/description, captured 2026-09-11); this Sep-14 reading matches achievement-tracker.html's live embedded list exactly and supersedes two OLDER on-site readings of the same 46 percentages that this pass deliberately did not carry into the achievement entities: trophies.html (read August 31, 2026) and inline 'September 7' figures quoted inside the individual boss-guide pages. All three readings are consistent with each other (percentages drift upward over time as more players progress) and the site itself explicitly frames this as drift, not disagreement -- so only the latest (Sep 14) reading is carried as each achievement's unlock_rate_pct; the boss-guide pages' own Aug31/Sep7 citations are left in place in those HTML pages and not reproduced field-by-field here. This entities.json has no zh locale field (unlike data/valheim/entities.json's name_zh): the Beast of Reincarnation subsite ships only en/de/es/fr/it/ja locales, no content/beast/*.md translation pack exists yet, and the ja/ locale mirror keeps boss/weapon proper nouns in Roman script rather than substituting an official localized name -- so there is no sourced translation to place in a name_zh field for boss/weapon/mechanic entities, and adding one as name_en==name_zh across every entity was judged to be pure noise rather than useful schema parity. name_ja IS included for achievements specifically, per this task's explicit instruction, because Steam's own Japanese achievement list is a genuine, directly-sourced official name distinct from the site's own page translations.

elemental-weaknesses.summary_en: The boss roster records 6 weakness labels (Flame, Poison, Lightning, Acid, Water, Explosive) across 11 story bosses, plus one boss (the finale) with no weakness. Only 3 elements are confirmed enchantable in the shipped build (Fire, Lightning, Wet). The two lists overlap in exactly 2 places (Fire~Flame on Rangifer; Lightning on Lacerta and Corvus) — everywhere else, the "counter" is a boss-reward ability line rather than something you can equip.

nushi-skills.summary_en: Boss rewards fall into 4 categories: Nushi Skill (5 total), named arts, Blade Arts (6 fights grant one), and Finishers (4 fights grant one, rarest label). All 5 Nushi Skills are unlocked by the end of Chapter 7 — nothing after that introduces a new Nushi Skill, only upgrades (rank II) and Finishers.
upgrade_only_rewards: Asagao: Boa II (Ursa, origin of rank I not documented)
Kiku: Bloom Strike II (Erymanth, origin of rank I not documented)
fights_with_no_new_reward: Crimson Malefact (Ch.9) — pure story wall, no Nushi Skill, no ability
Beast of Reincarnation (Ch.13) — "Blossoms of Reincarnation", type unspecified
routing_notes: Lacerta -> the Poison bosses: Dokuzeri line answers Shidou & Nue (Ch.3/6/11) and Kunai & Kirin (Ch.8/12) — 5 encounters answered by one Ch.2 reward.
Corvus -> the Acid bosses: Acid Burst Nobudou (Ch.7) answers the Taurus rematch (Ch.8) and Ursa (Ch.10).
Rangifer's Sakura Storm answers no later boss weakness — it is a general-purpose opener, not a routed counter.

disputed_double_credit.note: bosses.html's own reward table credits this Nushi Skill to BOTH the Nue Malefact (Ch.1/Ch.3) row and the Shidou & Nue (Ch.3) row; the weapons page lists it only under Shidou & Nue. The walkthrough calls the Nue Malefact's Ch.3 encounter as "feeding into" Chimeric Flow. No page states outright whether these are one event or two rewards.

combat-gauges.name_en: Combat Gauges (FP, Down Gauge, Entanglement Gauge)
combat-gauges.summary_en: Three meters, one verb: a clean parry pays into all three simultaneously. FP is Koo's shared resource pool; the Down Gauge belongs to the enemy and is a stagger/execution meter; the Entanglement Gauge is Emma's own and charges her Entanglement Overdrive burst.

gauges.note: The only one of the three gauges that keeps working when Koo is not with you (e.g. the Crimson Malefact fight).

spirit-stones.summary_en: Equippable collectibles that grant Emma additional stats and passive triggered effects (FP restoration on a parry, attack boosts at full HP, higher crit rate on executions, etc.). Found in overworld strongboxes and drops; some also purchasable from merchants and Brad at the Cleanse Walker.
spirit-stones.slots_note: 4 equippable in the early chapters, rising to 6 by the end of the game as more equipment slots unlock. Stated twice on the page (body text and FAQ), consistently.
acquisition: Purchasable from merchants and from Brad at the Cleanse Walker

stones.name: Fortification
stones.effect: Beginning a battle boosts Fortitude (which boosts defense for a time). Lv1-3: Fortitude +1 to +3.

stones.name: Onslaught
stones.effect: Beginning a battle boosts Vigor. Lv1-3: Vigor +1 to +3.

stones.name: Sharpshooter
stones.effect: Exploiting an enemy's elemental weakness with a ranged weapon has a chance to restore 1 FP to Koo. Recovery rate scales from +20% to +30% across 3 levels.

stones.name: Momentum
stones.effect: Boosts Emma and Koo's attack while Emma's HP is full. Scales from +5% to +10% across 5 levels.

stones.name: Homing Shots
stones.effect: Ranged projectiles gain tracking. Scales from Low to Full Tracking across 5 levels.

stones.name: Entangled Dodge
stones.effect: Dodging has a chance to restore Emma's Entanglement Gauge by 0.2 and Koo's FP by 1. Rate scales 10% to 50% across 5 levels.

stones.name: Well of Fortitude
stones.effect: Boosts Fortitude when Emma's HP drops below half. Lv1-3: Fortitude +1 to +3.

stones.name: Entangled Parry
stones.effect: Parrying has a chance to restore the Entanglement Gauge by 0.2 and Koo's FP by 1. Same 10%-50% scaling as Entangled Dodge.

stones.name: Entangled Assassination
stones.effect: Defeating an enemy with Death from Above or an Assassination restores both the Entanglement Gauge and Koo's FP.

stones.name: Entanglement Increase
stones.effect: Exploiting an elemental weakness has a chance to restore the Entanglement Gauge and Koo's FP. Rate scales from 3% to 7% across 5 levels.

stones.name: Florescent Recovery
stones.effect: Bloom Arts restore Emma and Koo's HP every second for 5 seconds. Lv1-3: HP Recovery 0.3% to 0.8%.

stones.name: Iron Wall
stones.effect: Reduces damage Emma takes, but cuts health recovery in half. Lv1-3: 15% to 25% damage reduction.

stones.name: Dark Approach
stones.effect: Boosts damage while Emma is unseen by enemies — a stealth-build stone. Scales 5% to 10% across 5 levels.

stones.name: Entanglement Stone
stones.effect: Combat begins with Emma's Entanglement Gauge and Koo's FP already increased. Lv1-3: +1/+1 to +3/+3.

stones.name: Critical Damage Increase
stones.effect: Boosts Emma and Koo's critical damage. Scales 5% to 25% across 5 levels.

stones.name: Final Breath
stones.effect: Performing an execution recovers Emma's HP. Recovery scales from 10% to 25% across 5 levels.

spirit-stones.stone_count_note: 16 stones have confirmed effect text on this page; the page does not claim this is an exhaustive list of every Spirit Stone in the game.
spirit-stones.level_cap_note: Most stones cap at Level 3, some go to Level 5, per the effect table. Each stone also carries flat HP/Skill Power/Defense/Critical Rate bonuses at Level 2 that the page says stack on top of the listed effect, without itemizing the numbers.
spirit-stones.blighted_variant_note: Several stones exist in a stronger Blighted variant that roughly doubles the flat stat bonus (example given: Onslaught's Blighted version doubles its Attack bonus from +6 to +12 at the equivalent level). Blighted stones are rarer overworld finds than their normal counterparts.
spirit-stones.duplication: Available at the Cleanse Walker's workbench for stones already owned; costs noticeably more Amber than finding or buying the stone again; cannot unlock new stones, only duplicate ones already in inventory.
spirit-stones.sell_guidance: Sell only when Amber is needed urgently, to Brad at the Cleanse Walker or overworld merchants. Firm rule stated: keep higher-rarity stones (hard to refind); sell common, easily-rebought stones first.
